summary: The construction and rank estimate are otherwise coherent, but the proof does not handle the possible case in which there are no bad parity classes, so its asserted strict bad-mass inequality is not established as written.
gaps: Equation (28) is claimed by summing the strict inequalities (27) over the bad classes. If the set of bad classes is empty, that summation yields only 0 = 0, not the asserted strict inequality P_bad < (1/2) sum_{xi bad} M_xi. The proof gives no separate empty-family argument, despite making the unconditional strict claim P_bad < G/2.
repair_hints: Split into cases. If at least one bad class exists, summing (27) is strict. If none exists, then P_bad = 0, while W > 0 implies sum_xi M_xi > 0 and (4) implies G > 0, hence P_bad = 0 < G/2.
